title: The Prestige
synopsis: Two magicians, a transported man, a tank of water, and a notebook that may be telling the truth or the better lie.

nodes.text: A trick gone wrong on a stage in front of strangers. You cannot avoid Funeral; you can only decide whether “Tie a slipknot” or “Use a true knot” defines the person who reaches it. In Sarah's Tank, waiting would only let someone else define what your silence meant.

choices.consequence: You commit to tie a slipknot. By Funeral, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.
You choose to use a true knot. It opens the route to Funeral, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: A bullet, a brother, a daughter handed back across a counter. The distance between The Prestige and The Beautiful Lie begins with the choice between “Take her home” and “Stay to burn.” A third choice, “Take the third path,” keeps The Cost in play.

choices.consequence: You take her home. The decision moves you toward The Prestige and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.
You choose to stay to burn. It opens the route to The Beautiful Lie, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.
Some endings reveal themselves last. You choose to take the third path. It opens the route to The Cost, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: You sit at last in front of a small girl who calls you Daddy and does not know which of you that is. You hold her hand. You agree, both of you, that it is.

Audiences fill the theater for a year. They want to be fooled. You give them their money's worth, again and again, until the lie wears thin and you sleep. The road into The Beautiful Lie began with “Stay to burn” in Workshop in Flames; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You publish the notebook. Magic, in your city, dies a little. So do you. So does Angier, in his way. The next century will reinvent both. The road into The Cost began with “Take the third path” in Workshop in Flames; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.
